title: Reading Test 7: Electric Buses and Urban Transport

passage.label: A
passage.text: Electric buses are being introduced in many cities as transport authorities attempt to reduce emissions from public transport. Unlike diesel buses, electric buses produce no exhaust fumes while driving, which can improve air quality along busy routes.

passage.label: B
passage.text: The environmental benefit of electric buses depends partly on how electricity is produced. If the electricity comes mainly from coal, the total reduction in emissions may be smaller. If it comes from renewable sources such as wind or solar power, the overall impact can be much stronger.

passage.label: C
passage.text: Electric buses can also be quieter than diesel vehicles. This is useful in residential streets and near schools, where traffic noise can affect daily life. However, quiet vehicles may create new safety concerns for pedestrians who rely on sound when crossing roads.

passage.label: D
passage.text: Charging infrastructure is one of the main practical challenges. Bus operators need charging points at depots or along routes, and schedules must allow enough time for batteries to recharge. In cold weather or on hilly routes, batteries may lose energy more quickly.

passage.label: E
passage.text: Although electric buses can be expensive to purchase, their running costs may be lower because electricity and maintenance can cost less than diesel fuel and engine repairs. For many cities, the decision involves balancing high initial costs against long-term savings and environmental goals.
